newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 24.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- Defence Minister Joe Modise and National Conventional Arms Control Committee chairman Professor Kader Asmal have admitted that South Africa is supplying arms to Uganda, which is alleged to be the main supporter of Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila.

- The government would have to mobilise the nation's resources, including those of the private sector, to prevent the disintegration of the public service in certain provinces, public service director-general Paseka Ncholo warned.

- A group of Sentrachem Ltd's minority shareholders is to sue the chemicals company in the Johannesburg High Court, alleging that it failed to disclose significant losses arising from ill-judged forward cover contracts at subsidiary Sanachem in good time.

- Durban municipal authorities have backed down from their blanket opposition to land restoration in Cato Manor, where inner city development projects valued at between four to five billion rand have been earmarked, by conceding to former Group Areas Act victims that they may get their land back if this is "feasible", sources said on Wednesday.

- Afrikaner Resistance Movement (AWB) leader Eugene Terre'Blanche was convicted on Wedensday of trying to murder Paul Motshabi, 27, who suffered brain damage in a beating in March last year, and of assaulting another black employee.
BUSINESS REPORT

- The Compass Group Plc, a British-based contract caterer, has bought a 40 percent stake in South Africa's Kagiso Khulani Supervision Food Services for 133,4 million rand, the two groups said on Wednesday.

- The government was rushing through amendments to customs legislation in a last-ditch attempt to plug loopholes in the Southern African Customs Union believed to be costing the fiscus hundreds of millions of rands, officials said on Wednesday.
- South Africa's first casino licence was granted to Global Resorts on Wednesday for a new casino complex in Secunda in Mpumalanga.
- South Africa may be one of the bigger trading nations of the world but it is not one of the most dynamic, the World Trade Organisation (WTO) said recently.

- Consumer inflation dropped to 9,6 percent in March from 9,8 percent in February, figures released by the Central Statistical Service on Wednesday showed, prompting analysts to revise their forecasts for inflation at the year-end marginally downwards.
SAKE BEELD
- The lower inflation rate in March from February prompts some economists to say the upwards trend from previous months is almost nearing a turning point.
- Boland Bank Holdings Ltd records outstanding performance with year-end results to end March with attributable earnings up 47 percent to 112,9 million rand.
THE STAR
- House of Assembly Deputy Speaker Baleka Kgositsile's driver's licence was invalid, the Moldenhauer Commission of Inquiry heard on Wednesday.
- South Africa's national soccer side Bafana Bafana are in demand worldwide and are firmly establishing themselves as global players.

- In a past era AWB leader Eugene TerreBlanche threatened war to stop democratic change in its tracks, but on Wednesday he blustered and wept when a Potchefstroom Magistrate's Court found him guilty of trying to kill one of his black workers and of assaulting another.

- The exercise to compile a register of fixed state assets has unearthed 12,000 government-owned properties valued at close to one billion rand which were not known, Public Works Minister Jeff Radebe announced in Parliament on Wednesday.
- Filmmaker Teddy Mattera, 33, the son of well-known poet Don Mattera, appeared in the Johannesburg Magistrate's Court on Wednesday on a rape charge.
